I want to clarify, my hours currently on Steam do not reflect my actual playtime, as I've played this game both pirated (yes, I know) and on Switch. 



UNDERTALE is without a doubt my favorite game of all time.
I've been a massive fan of this game since its release. I've played both major routes, (at time of reviewing) Pacifist twice and Genocide three times, and it still gives me the same feelings as the first time I've ever played it.

A game about choices mattering, a bundle of characters and dialogue options that interact with you, fun fights and gameplay mechanics, and a beautiful story that keeps me hooked to this very day. 

My PROS:

- If you love RPG style games, UNDERTALE delivers a great one. It may not be technically flashy, especially compared to what is being made nowadays, but it's still really well done.
- The story. It's about what makes someone human and what makes someone a monster. It makes you think about your choices, care for the characters, and really hammers home points in such a well-written fashion that I cry every time I play its happiest ending.
- "Despite everything, it's still you."
- Memorable characters and boss fights. If the normal enemies don't stick with you, the main bosses will. Each one has its own unique spin, a personality that clings to you like glue. I GUARENTEE you will have a favorite boss, even if you don't enjoy the game as much as you thought.
- Toby "One Song" "Radiation" Fox created, in my opinion the best soundtrack ever. Fight music is catchy, environment background music is catchy, BOSS MUSIC is so INCREDIBLY catchy. It's GOOD. GREAT even. 

CONS!

- If you aren't a fan of 8-bit style games, probably don't think about it lmao. Unless you want to try one, in this case give UNDERTALE a fair go around.
- Toby Fox built this game on spaghetti noodles, so expect some of your inputs to be a bit behind or unfair in some fights. 
- No volume slider.
- It's quite short, despite how long you feel you're playing for. If yo…

It’s no wonder that this game received so much popularity upon its release back in 2015, and it still isn’t shocking that it’s managed to maintain that popularity for a decade and running. Undertale just possesses a unique liveliness and charm that can’t really be found in many other places.  This game is just brimming with some of the most lively and heartwarming characters out there, and it’s this fact that makes your choices so much more intriguing.

Undertale is built upon one simple question: ‘Will you manipulate others to forge your own path or will you find a way to press on without harming those around you?’ The whimsical vibe of Undertale’s underground world makes the player think harder about the consequences of their decisions. What really stands out as brilliant to me is how this game is built entirely around this central question. The environments and characters are intentionally charming and love able in order to invoke the player to feel a certain way towards them.

Even the gameplay manages to fit this motif. Undertale is built upon the same basic framework of early SNES rpg games, but it expands upon the concept by giving the player more freedom to do to the approaching enemy as he pleases. This freedom of choice even extends to the way the player is attacked. When you are attacked by an enemy you are forced into a short bullet hell minigame, which gives the player the ability to dodge attacks in a unique sense. It’s a lovely way to add skill to the mix in order to stop the player from being incapable to defend himself. Undertale presents you with a world full of liveliness and it gives you the freedom to do to it as you please.

The major thing that Undertale does so well is the way that its story is clearly woven into every choice the developer made. Everything exists with intention, and the game never feels repetitive because each new addition as you progress adds something fundamentally important.

I've played a lot of games over the years, but very few have stayed with me the way Undertale has. It's one of those games that's incredibly difficult to describe without making it sound bigger than it is, because on the surface it's just a small indie RPG with simple pixel art and a short runtime. What makes it special isn't its graphics or its mechanics on their own, it's how every part of the game works together to create something that feels genuine.

The writing is probably its strongest aspect. Every character has their own personality and purpose, and none of them feel like they're only there to move the story forward. Even the smallest interactions have charm behind them, and the game somehow manages to balance humor with serious moments without either feeling forced. It never tries too hard to make you laugh or to make you cry, it just lets its characters exist naturally.

The combat is another reason why the game stands out. Instead of being another turn based RPG where every encounter feels the same, Undertale constantly changes things up. Every enemy has different attack patterns, different dialogue, and different ways to approach the fight. The option to spare enemies instead of killing them isn't just a gimmick either. It's built into the game's identity and completely changes how you experience the story.

What I appreciate most about Undertale is how it respects the player. It doesn't constantly explain itself or hold your hand. It trusts you to pay attention, to notice details, and to think about the choices you're making. Almost everything you do has some kind of consequence, and the game remembers far more than you'd expect. Because of that, every route feels intentional rather than just being a different ending.

The soundtrack deserves just as much praise. Almost every track is memorable, and Toby Fox does an incredible job of reusing melodies throughout the game to connect different characters and moments. Even years later, there are so…

Some of the best characters - memorable and instantly endearing the moment you see them - one of the best storylines, and amazing music. A one-of-a-kind masterpiece that changed the world of video games, reminding us that masterpieces can still be created using nothing but pixel art. And all of this was created by just one person... 10/10

Undertale is a unique RPG with memorable characters, a fantastic soundtrack, and a combat system that stands out from almost everything else in the genre. The emotional moments hit hard, and your choices genuinely matter.

That said, I don't think it's flawless. Some sections felt unnecessarily slow, almost as if they were designed just to stretch the game's length rather than add meaningful content. There were moments where I found myself wanting to move on instead of being engaged.

I also wish the lore had been explored much further within Undertale itself. The world has so much potential, but it often feels like it only scratches the surface, leaving me wanting more background and world-building.

Another personal impression I had was that parts of the gameplay and bullet-pattern battles reminded me a lot of the Touhou series. While Undertale puts its own spin on them, a few moments felt heavily inspired by that style.

Overall, it's still a game I'd recommend because of its originality, music, characters, and emotional impact. I just don't think it's quite the untouchable masterpiece that many people make it out to be.

7/10

Undertale is one of those rare games that completely lives up to its reputation.it quickly becomes something memorable. The writing is funny, emotional, and surprisingly deep, while every character feels unique and genuinely memorable.

The combat system stands out because you don't have to solve every encounter with violence. Choosing to spare enemies completely changes the experience and makes every decision feel meaningful. The game constantly plays with your expectations and uses its mechanics in creative ways that few RPGs even attempt.

The soundtrack is incredible, with tracks that perfectly match every moment, from lighthearted scenes to emotional climaxes. Combined with the charming pixel art, it creates an atmosphere that's hard to forget.

What really makes Undertale special is how it connects gameplay with its story. Your actions matter, and the game remembers them, making each route feel personal rather than just offering different endings.

It's not perfect—some puzzles are a bit simple, and the graphics won't appeal to everyone—but those are small complaints compared to everything the game does so well.

Undertale is funny, heartfelt, clever, and unforgettable. Whether you're a fan of RPGs or not, it's a game that deserves to be experienced at least once.
